item.research_question: How can the strength–ductility synergy in eutectic high-entropy alloys be improved by inheriting the composite lamellar nature through tailored thermo-mechanical processing?
item.processing_route: Arc-melting followed by suction-casting into a copper mold, multi-pass cold-rolling to 84–86% reduction in thickness, and non-isothermal annealing at 660, 700, 740, or 900 °C for 1 h with a heating rate of 10 °C min−1 followed by water quenching.
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile tests with an initial strain rate of 2.5 × 10−4 s−1 using dog-bone specimens (15 mm gauge length, 3.2 mm width, 600 μm thickness) and loading–unloading–reloading (LUR) tests.
key_findings: The DPHL700 and DPHL740 samples achieved a yield strength of approximately 1.5 GPa with an elongation of ~16%, representing a simultaneous enhancement in both strength and ductility compared to as-cast and ultrafine-grained counterparts.
The microstructure exhibited a two-hierarchical heterogeneity consisting of submicron-grade FCC/B2 grains within FCC lamellae and micron-grade alternate FCC/B2 lamellae.
The average diameters of FCC and B2 grains were roughly comparable at ~0.71 μm, with inter-lamella spacings ranging from 1.5 to 5 μm.
Phase decomposition resulted in two types of NiAl-rich precipitates in FCC lamellae: small intragranular P1 grains (50–180 nm) and large intergranular P2 grains (~350 nm).
Back-stress measurements at the yield point reached ~950 MPa, which was approximately 3 times higher than the effective stress, primarily responsible for the high yield strength.
The strain-hardening rate (Θ) showed a transient behavior with an up-turn in region II and sustained high Θ over a wide strain region III for DPHL700.
Microcrack-arresting mechanisms were observed where multiple microcracks were inhibited from coalescing, with ductile components acting as efficient crack arresters.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the enhanced properties to a two-hierarchical constraint effect that generates long-range back-stress by storing geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) due to strain gradients at lamella interfaces and around intergranular precipitates, combined with a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism where the aligned lamellar architecture delays crack propagation and coalescence.
item.limitations: The authors note that while the DPHL structure is effective, increasing the annealing temperature to 900 °C induced a partially degraded lamellar structure that led to inferior tensile properties, indicating the sensitivity of the process to thermal treatment.
item.future_work: The authors propose that further efforts should be devoted to exploring non-equiatomic alloys and spinodal decomposition to create low-misfit coherent nanostructures for even higher yield strengths, and anticipate modifying the EHEA to satisfy requirements for high-temperature and/or corrosion environments.
quotes: The as-prepared samples exhibit hierarchically-structural heterogeneity due to phase decomposition, and the improved mechanical response during deformation is attributed to both a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.

The back-stress (~950 MPa) of the closest to yield point is ~3 times higher than the effective stress in DPHL700, which quantitatively explains that the larger back-stress is primarily responsible for the observed high yield strength.

The ductile components such as the FCC matrix, and even the hard B2 lamellae in the current samples, will therefore work well as very efficient crack arresters to delay crack propagation and coalescence during deformation.
